evals.name: explicit-dotnet-agent-prereq-check
evals.prompt: Check prerequisites for .NET agents. I'm planning a coordinator agent with two specialists using Microsoft Agent Framework on Dapr Workflow, backed by Anthropic.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the OS, then checks the C# LSP plugin, .NET 10 SDK, Docker/Podman, Dapr CLI and the LLM providers in parallel. API keys are reported only as set/unset. If everything passes it points to create-agent-dotnet. No Python checks are run.
expectations: Runs `uname -s` (OS detection) before the other checks
Runs `dotnet --version` (requiring major version 10 or higher), `docker info` (or `podman info`) and `dapr --version`
Probes OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and GOOGLE_API_KEY as set/unset, and probes Ollama at http://localhost:11434/api/tags
No API key value appears in any command output or in the final message
Does not run `python --version`, `uv --version` or `uv pip show dapr-agents`
Final report lists C# LSP plugin, .NET SDK, Docker/Podman, Dapr CLI and LLM provider each with a pass or fail status; if all pass it names the `create-agent-dotnet` skill
Does not create any files and does not run `dotnet new` or `dotnet add package`

evals.name: casual-csharp-agent-gemini
evals.prompt: can i build a durable AI agent in c# with dapr on this laptop? i'd use gemini. is there a dapr agents nuget i need?
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the .NET agent prerequisite check. It checks GOOGLE_API_KEY as set/unset along with the other providers. It explains that Dapr Agents is Python-only and that the .NET path is Microsoft Agent Framework on Dapr Workflow via Diagrid.AI.Microsoft.AgentFramework, so there is no Dapr Agents NuGet to check.
expectations: Runs `dotnet --version`, `dapr --version` and `docker info` (or `podman info`) rather than answering from general knowledge
Probes GOOGLE_API_KEY with a set/unset test and does not print its value
States that Dapr Agents is a Python-only framework and that .NET uses Microsoft Agent Framework with the `Diagrid.AI.Microsoft.AgentFramework` package
Does not try to look up, check for, or install a .NET 'Dapr Agents' package
Treats the LLM provider check as passing if any one provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or Ollama) is available

evals.name: windows-no-llm-provider
evals.prompt: I'm on Windows with PowerShell. Verify my .NET agent environment. I haven't set up any LLM API keys yet and I'm not running Ollama.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs every check. On Windows it uses or falls back to the PowerShell forms of the probes. It reports keys only as set/unset. If no provider is available it marks the LLM check failed and lists the four options with their links. The other checks are still reported and nothing is installed.
expectations: Probes each key with either the POSIX test or the PowerShell form `powershell -Command "if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($env:OPENAI_API_KEY)) { 'unset' } else { 'set' }"` (same pattern for ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and GOOGLE_API_KEY)
Does not use `printenv`, `echo $VAR`, or a bare `$env:VAR` expression to inspect a key

If no probe succeeds, the LLM check is reported as failed and lists OPENAI_API_KEY (platform.openai.com), ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (console.anthropic.com), GOOGLE_API_KEY (ai.google.dev) and Ollama (`ollama serve`)
Still reports results for the .NET SDK, Docker/Podman, Dapr CLI and C# LSP plugin checks
Does not set environment variables, write a `.env` file, or install Ollama
